arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: the side that brought the case asserts the specific statute provides a different rule for costs.
the opposing side asserts the general rule applies unless expressly repealed by statute.
Justice Breyer questioned the legislative intent behind the specific statutory language.
Justice Sotomayor asked if the specific statute meets the requirement for express repeal.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case tests the interaction between a specific federal statute and a general procedural rule. The core issue is whether the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act displaces the default rule for cost awards.

paragraphs: This case determines whether prevailing defendants in debt collection suits can recover court costs. The outcome affects the financial burden on debt collectors and the scope of judicial discretion in awarding costs.
